test_title: PYST 29: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which one of the following is NOT an agent of cross pollination?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Light**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cross-pollination**, also known as **allogamy**, involves the transfer of **pollen grains** from the **anther** of a flower of one plant to the **stigma** of a flower of another plant of the same species.
 
• To facilitate this transfer over a distance, plants rely on various **pollinating agents**, which are broadly classified into **abiotic** (non-living) and **biotic** (living) agents.
 
• **Wind** is a common **abiotic agent** of cross-pollination. Plants that use wind for pollination, such as **grasses**, **corn**, and many **conifers**, produce large quantities of light, non-sticky pollen. *Hence, statement 4 is a correct agent.*
 
• **Water** is another **abiotic agent**, primarily used by aquatic plants like **Vallisneria** and **Hydrilla**. In these cases, pollen grains are often long and needle-like to float and reach the stigma. *Hence, statement 2 is a correct agent.*
 
• **Animals** serve as the primary **biotic agents**. This includes **insects** (bees, butterflies), **birds** (sunbirds, hummingbirds), and **mammals** (bats). These animals are attracted to the flower's **nectar**, **color**, or **scent**. *Hence, statement 3 is a correct agent.*
 
• **Light** is an essential environmental factor for **photosynthesis** and **photoperiodism** (the physiological reaction of organisms to the length of night or day). While light influences **flowering time**, it does not act as a physical carrier to transport pollen grains from one plant to another. *Hence, statement 1 is NOT an agent of cross-pollination.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anemophily (Wind Pollination):**

 
 
• Flowers are generally small, **inconspicuous**, and lack **nectar** or **scent**.
 
• The **pollen grains** are **light**, **dry**, and **smooth-walled** so they can be easily carried by the wind.
 
• The **stigma** is often **feathery** or **branched** to catch the airborne pollen.
 
 
 
• **Hydrophily (Water Pollination):**
 
 
• This is relatively rare, occurring in only about **30 genera** of **monocotyledons**.
 
• Pollen grains are protected from wetting by a **mucilaginous covering**.
 
 
 
• **Zoophily (Animal Pollination):**
 
 
• **Entomophily** refers specifically to pollination by **insects**. These flowers are usually **brightly colored** and **fragrant**.
 
• **Ornithophily** is pollination by **birds**, while **Chiropterophily** is pollination by **bats**.
 
• Pollinators receive a "reward" in the form of **pollen** or **nectar**.
 
 
 
• **Self-Pollination vs. Cross-Pollination:**
 
 
• **Self-pollination** (Autogamy) occurs within the same flower or between flowers of the same plant.
 
• **Cross-pollination** increases **genetic diversity** and leads to the production of stronger, more adaptable offspring.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Light's Role:** It is important to distinguish that **Light** triggers the **biological clock** of a plant to start the **reproductive phase**, but the actual transport of genetic material (pollen) requires a physical medium like air, water, or a living creature.
 
• **Evolutionary Adaptation:** Many plants have evolved specific **morphological features** to favor cross-pollination over self-pollination, such as **Dichogamy** (different maturation times of anther and stigma) or **Self-incompatibility**.
